## Explanation of the task 1

Task 1 examined whether adding uncertainty information made the underlying spatial
pattern in an EEG topoplot more difficult to recognize. On each trial, participants
saw a target ERP pattern and two alternative topoplots. They selected the alternative
that most closely matched the target. One alternative represented the same ERP-pattern
class as the target, while the other represented a different class.

The task included three characteristic ERP patterns: MMN, P3, and N170. Each was
shown using each of the seven visualization types. This produced 21 trials per
participant, each on separate page. Trial order was randomized separately for every
participant.

![Example comparison trial. Participants selected the alternative whose spatial pattern
most closely matched the target.](<../The Art of Uncertain Topoplots/figures/task1_explainer.png>){#fig-task1-explainer width=100% fig-alt="A target EEG topoplot above two alternative topoplots. A selection marker indicates that the participant chooses the alternative whose spatial pattern best matches the target."}


```{r shared-setup}
#| include: false
source("scripts/analysis_setup.R")
```

## Trial reconstruction and presentation order

- Trial information was reconstructed from the survey records and joined with each
  participant's responses using participant, trial, and question identifiers.

```{r}
task1_order <- data %>%
  dplyr::select(ID, A125_02) %>%
  tidyr::separate_rows(A125_02, sep = "\n") %>%
  dplyr::filter(A125_02 != "") %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    ID,
    position = as.integer(get_field(A125_02, "position")),
    trial    = as.integer(get_field(A125_02, "trial")),
    question = get_field(A125_02, "question"),
    stimulus = get_field(A125_02, "stimulus"),
    expected = as.integer(get_field(A125_02, "expected")),
    answered = as.integer(get_field(A125_02, "answered")),
    correct  = as.integer(get_field(A125_02, "correct"))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(ID, position)

task1_design <- data %>%
  dplyr::select(ID, A124_01) %>%
  tidyr::separate_rows(A124_01, sep = "\n") %>%
  dplyr::filter(A124_01 != "") %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    ID,
    trial       = as.integer(get_field(A124_01, "trial")),
    question    = get_field(A124_01, "question"),
    vistype     = get_field(A124_01, "vistype"),
    target      = get_field(A124_01, "target"),
    correct     = get_field(A124_01, "correct"),
    wrong       = get_field(A124_01, "wrong"),
    pair        = get_field(A124_01, "pair"),
    solution    = as.integer(get_field(A124_01, "solution")),
    opt1        = get_field(A124_01, "opt1"),
    opt2        = get_field(A124_01, "opt2")
  )

task1 <- task1_order %>%
  left_join(
    task1_design %>%
      transmute(
        ID,
        trial,
        question,
        vistype,
        pattern = target,
        correct_image = correct,
        wrong_image = wrong,
        pair,
        solution,
        opt1,
        opt2
      ),
    by = c("ID", "trial", "question")
  )
```

## Accuracy analysis

- Every response was coded as correct (`1`) or incorrect (`0`).

- The analysis contains 2,394 responses: 114 participants × 21 trials.

- Visualization type was treated as a categorical variable, with the basic topoplot as
  the reference condition.

- Presentation position was represented by the centered variable `position_c`,
  calculated as `position - mean(position)`. Because positions ranged from 1 to 21,
  their mean was 11. Thus, `position_c = 0` represents position 11, negative values
  represent earlier trials, and positive values represent later trials. This variable
  tests whether accuracy changed linearly as participants progressed through the task.

- No responses were excluded for missing values. All 2,394 reconstructed records
  contained accuracy, visualization type, ERP pattern, presentation position, target
  stimulus, and distractor stimulus.

- Stimulus assignment was incomplete but overlapping across participants. Across their
  21 trials, participants saw 12--20 unique target stimuli (median 16), 13--20 unique
  distractors (median 15), and 18--28 unique stimulus identities across both roles
  (median 23). No participant saw all 30 stimulus identities. Because specific targets
  and distractors may differ in difficulty, this design motivates separate target- and
  distractor-stimulus random intercepts in the inferential model.

```{r}
task1_model <- task1 %>%
  transmute(
    ID = factor(ID),
    trial = factor(trial),
    vistype = relevel(factor(vistype), ref = "basic"),
    pattern = relevel(factor(pattern), ref = "MMN"),
    stimulus = factor(stimulus),
    wrong_image = factor(wrong_image),
    position = as.integer(position),
    correct = as.integer(correct)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(correct),
    !is.na(position),
    !is.na(vistype),
    !is.na(pattern),
    !is.na(stimulus),
    !is.na(wrong_image)
  ) %>%
  mutate(position_c = position - mean(position))
```

### Observed accuracy

- Accuracy was calculated as correct responses divided by all responses
  (`correct / (correct + incorrect)`). Each visualization type had 342 responses
  (114 participants × 3 trials). This is an unadjusted pooled proportion.

- For the descriptive uncertainty display, each participant contributed one mean
  accuracy per visualization type, calculated from their three trials. Because every
  participant contributed the same number of trials, the across-participant mean equals
  the pooled proportion above.

- The dark-blue region shows the two-sided 95% *t*-confidence interval around the
  across-participant mean; opacity decreases beyond that interval.

```{r}
task1_gradient_participants <- task1_model |>
  group_by(ID, vistype) |>
  summarise(
    participant_accuracy = mean(correct),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

task1_gradient_order <- task1_gradient_participants |>
  group_by(vistype) |>
  summarise(mean_accuracy = mean(participant_accuracy), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(mean_accuracy) |>
  pull(vistype) |>
  as.character()

task1_gradient_summary <- task1_gradient_participants |>
  group_by(vistype) |>
  summarise(
    n_participants = n(),
    mean_accuracy = mean(participant_accuracy),
    se_accuracy = sd(participant_accuracy) / sqrt(n_participants),
    df = n_participants - 1,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    vistype = factor(vistype, levels = task1_gradient_order),
    y_position = as.numeric(vistype),
    lower_95 = mean_accuracy - qt(0.975, df) * se_accuracy,
    upper_95 = mean_accuracy + qt(0.975, df) * se_accuracy
  ) |>
  arrange(vistype)

task1_response_counts <- task1_model |>
  group_by(vistype) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_correct = sum(correct == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_incorrect = sum(correct == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    pooled_accuracy = mean(correct, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

vistype_table <- task1_response_counts |>
  left_join(
    task1_gradient_summary |>
      select(vistype, mean_accuracy, lower_95, upper_95),
    by = "vistype"
  )

stopifnot(
  all(task1_gradient_summary$n_participants == n_distinct(task1_model$ID)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    vistype_table$pooled_accuracy,
    vistype_table$mean_accuracy,
    tolerance = 1e-12
  ))
)

vistype_table |>
  mutate(
    vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
    mean_accuracy = scales::percent(mean_accuracy, accuracy = 0.1),
    lower_95 = scales::percent(lower_95, accuracy = 0.1),
    upper_95 = scales::percent(upper_95, accuracy = 0.1)
  ) |>
  select(-pooled_accuracy) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    col.names = c(
      "Visualization type",
      "Responses",
      "Correct",
      "Incorrect",
      "Mean accuracy",
      "Lower 95% CI",
      "Upper 95% CI"
    ),
    caption = "Observed comparison-task accuracy by visualization type",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```

```{r task1-descriptive-gradient-plot}
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Observed comparison-task accuracy summarized from participant-level means.
#|   Each participant contributes one mean from three trials per visualization type.
#|   The black line and label show the across-participant mean; the dark-blue region
#|   shows its two-sided 95% t-confidence interval. This unadjusted description does
#|   not replace the mixed model below, which accounts for ERP pattern, presentation
#|   position, participant, target stimulus, and distractor stimulus.

task1_gradient_data <- task1_gradient_summary |>
  tidyr::crossing(accuracy = seq(0.60, 0.90, length.out = 241)) |>
  mutate(
    t_distance = abs(accuracy - mean_accuracy) / se_accuracy,
    confidence_level = 2 * pt(t_distance, df) - 1,
    gradient_alpha = if_else(
      confidence_level <= 0.95,
      1,
      pmax(0, (1 - confidence_level) / 0.05)
    )
  )

task1_gradient_figure <- ggplot(
  task1_gradient_data,
  aes(x = accuracy, y = y_position)
) +
  geom_tile(
    aes(alpha = gradient_alpha),
    width = 1 / 800,
    height = 0.62,
    fill = "#6BAED6"
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = task1_gradient_summary,
    aes(
      x = mean_accuracy,
      xend = mean_accuracy,
      y = y_position - 0.31,
      yend = y_position + 0.31
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linewidth = 0.8,

  ) +

  ) +

    "Participant-level mean accuracy",
    limits = c(0.60, 0.90),
    breaks = seq(0.60, 0.90, 0.10),
    labels = scales::label_percent(),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = task1_gradient_summary$y_position,
    labels = unname(
      vistype_labels[as.character(task1_gradient_summary$vistype)]
    ),

  ) +
```

### Population-average accuracy

- A logistic mixed-effects model estimated the probability of a correct response:

  ```r
  correct ~ vistype + pattern + position_c +
    (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image)
  ```

- Some participants were generally more accurate than others. Because every participant
  completed 21 trials, we added a participant random intercept, which allows each
  participant to have their own baseline accuracy. The model then examines whether
  accuracy changed with visualization type or trial position across participants.

- ERP pattern was included as a fixed effect, so visualization comparisons account for
  systematic accuracy differences among MMN, N170, and P3 trials.

- Target and distractor stimuli were included as separate random intercepts. This gives
  each image its own baseline difficulty in each role and prevents unusually easy or
  difficult images from being mistaken for visualization effects.

- These probabilities estimate average accuracy for each visualization type across the
  modeled participant and stimulus populations. They were calculated at the average
  trial position, averaged equally across the three ERP patterns, and integrated over
  modeled differences among participants, target stimuli, and distractor stimuli.

```{r}
#| include: false

# Logistic mixed-effects model
task1_fit <- glmer(
  correct ~ vistype + pattern + position_c +
    (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image),
  data = task1_model,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)

# Check whether the data support a participant-specific presentation-position slope.
task1_position_slope_fit <- glmer(
  correct ~ vistype + pattern + position_c +
    (1 + position_c | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image),
  data = task1_model,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)
task1_position_slope_variance <- as.numeric(
  lme4::VarCorr(task1_position_slope_fit)$ID["position_c", "position_c"]
)
task1_position_slope_correlation <- as.numeric(
  attr(lme4::VarCorr(task1_position_slope_fit)$ID, "correlation")[
    "(Intercept)", "position_c"
  ]
)
task1_position_slope_singular <- lme4::isSingular(
  task1_position_slope_fit,
  tol = 1e-4
)

# Predictions are evaluated for every visualization-pattern combination and then
# averaged equally over the three experimentally controlled ERP patterns.
task1_vistype_levels <- levels(task1_model$vistype)
task1_pattern_levels <- levels(task1_model$pattern)
task1_prediction_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  vistype = factor(task1_vistype_levels, levels = task1_vistype_levels),
  pattern = factor(task1_pattern_levels, levels = task1_pattern_levels),
  position_c = 0
)

task1_average_over_patterns <- function(values) {
  vapply(
    task1_vistype_levels,
    function(visualization) {
      mean(values[as.character(task1_prediction_grid$vistype) == visualization])
    },
    numeric(1)
  )
}

task1_random_effect_sds <- function(model) {
  variance_components <- lme4::VarCorr(model)
  vapply(
    c("ID", "stimulus", "wrong_image"),
    function(group) as.numeric(attr(variance_components[[group]], "stddev")),
    numeric(1)
  )
}

# Population-average probabilities integrate over the fitted participant, target,
# and distractor random-intercept distributions. Their independent normal random
# intercepts sum to one normal distribution with the summed variance.
task1_population_probabilities <- function(model) {
  fixed_formula <- lme4::nobars(formula(model))
  fixed_terms <- delete.response(terms(fixed_formula))
  design_matrix <- model.matrix(fixed_terms, task1_prediction_grid)
  linear_predictor <- as.numeric(design_matrix %*% lme4::fixef(model))
  total_random_sd <- sqrt(sum(task1_random_effect_sds(model)^2))

  if (total_random_sd < sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)) {
    return(task1_average_over_patterns(plogis(linear_predictor)))
  }

  grid_probabilities <- vapply(
    linear_predictor,
    function(eta) {
      integrate(
        function(random_intercept) {
          plogis(eta + random_intercept) *
            dnorm(random_intercept, sd = total_random_sd)
        },
        lower = -Inf,
        upper = Inf,
        rel.tol = 1e-10
      )$value
    },
    numeric(1)
  )

  task1_average_over_patterns(grid_probabilities)
}

# Compare the three candidate summaries before selecting the reporting target.
task1_fixed_formula <- lme4::nobars(formula(task1_fit))
task1_fixed_terms <- delete.response(terms(task1_fixed_formula))
task1_design_matrix <- model.matrix(task1_fixed_terms, task1_prediction_grid)
task1_linear_predictor <- as.numeric(
  task1_design_matrix %*% lme4::fixef(task1_fit)
)
task1_participant_effects <- lme4::ranef(task1_fit)$ID[, 1]
task1_target_effects <- lme4::ranef(task1_fit)$stimulus[, 1]
task1_distractor_effects <- lme4::ranef(task1_fit)$wrong_image[, 1]
task1_fitted_random_effect_sums <- as.vector(
  outer(
    task1_participant_effects,
    as.vector(outer(task1_target_effects, task1_distractor_effects, "+")),
    "+"
  )
)

task1_conditional_probabilities <- task1_average_over_patterns(
  plogis(task1_linear_predictor)
)
task1_fitted_sample_probabilities <- task1_average_over_patterns(
  vapply(
    task1_linear_predictor,
    function(eta) mean(plogis(eta + task1_fitted_random_effect_sums)),
    numeric(1)
  )
)

task1_estimand_comparison <- tibble::tibble(
  vistype = factor(task1_vistype_levels, levels = task1_vistype_levels),
  conditional = task1_conditional_probabilities,
  fitted_sample = task1_fitted_sample_probabilities,
  population_average = task1_population_probabilities(task1_fit)
)

# Simulate fixed-effect uncertainty, then marginalize every draw over the fitted
# participant and stimulus distributions. This is much faster than model refitting.
set.seed(20261102)
task1_fixed_effect_draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(
  n = 10000,
  mu = lme4::fixef(task1_fit),
  Sigma = as.matrix(vcov(task1_fit))
)
task1_linear_predictor_draws <-
  task1_fixed_effect_draws %*% t(task1_design_matrix)
task1_random_effect_sd <- sqrt(sum(task1_random_effect_sds(task1_fit)^2))

# Twenty-point Gauss-Hermite quadrature accurately integrates the logistic-normal
# probabilities for all coefficient draws without model refitting.
task1_quadrature_order <- 20
task1_quadrature_matrix <- matrix(
  0,
  task1_quadrature_order,
  task1_quadrature_order
)
task1_quadrature_off_diagonal <- sqrt(
  seq_len(task1_quadrature_order - 1) / 2
)
task1_quadrature_matrix[
  cbind(
    seq_len(task1_quadrature_order - 1),
    2:task1_quadrature_order
  )
] <- task1_quadrature_off_diagonal
task1_quadrature_matrix[
  cbind(
    2:task1_quadrature_order,
    seq_len(task1_quadrature_order - 1)
  )
] <- task1_quadrature_off_diagonal
task1_quadrature <- eigen(task1_quadrature_matrix, symmetric = TRUE)
task1_quadrature_nodes <- task1_quadrature$values
task1_quadrature_weights <- task1_quadrature$vectors[1, ]^2

task1_population_draws_grid <- matrix(
  0,
  nrow = nrow(task1_linear_predictor_draws),
  ncol = ncol(task1_linear_predictor_draws)
)
for (quadrature_index in seq_along(task1_quadrature_nodes)) {
  task1_population_draws_grid <- task1_population_draws_grid +
    task1_quadrature_weights[quadrature_index] *
    plogis(
      task1_linear_predictor_draws +
        sqrt(2) * task1_random_effect_sd *
        task1_quadrature_nodes[quadrature_index]
    )
}

task1_population_draws <- vapply(
  task1_vistype_levels,
  function(visualization) {
    rowMeans(
      task1_population_draws_grid[
        , as.character(task1_prediction_grid$vistype) == visualization,
        drop = FALSE
      ]
    )
  },
  numeric(nrow(task1_population_draws_grid))
)

task1_probability_intervals <- apply(
  task1_population_draws,
  2,
  quantile,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

accuracy_estimates <- tibble::tibble(
  vistype = factor(task1_vistype_levels, levels = task1_vistype_levels),
  accuracy = task1_estimand_comparison$population_average,
  lower_ci = task1_probability_intervals[1, ],
  upper_ci = task1_probability_intervals[2, ]
) |>
  arrange(desc(accuracy)) |>
  mutate(
    vistype = factor(vistype, levels = rev(vistype))
  )

task1_conditional_gap <- max(abs(
  task1_estimand_comparison$population_average -
    task1_estimand_comparison$conditional
))
task1_sample_gap <- max(abs(
  task1_estimand_comparison$population_average -
    task1_estimand_comparison$fitted_sample
))
task1_conditional_gap_label <- sprintf(
  "%.1f percentage points",
  100 * task1_conditional_gap
)
task1_sample_gap_label <- sprintf(
  "%.1f percentage points",
  100 * task1_sample_gap
)
```

::: {.callout-note title="Choosing how to summarize predicted accuracy" collapse="true"}
There are three ways to summarize the model:

| Option | Calculation | What it describes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Set participant and stimulus differences to zero. | Average-baseline participants and stimuli. |
| 2 | Average over the fitted participants, targets, and distractors. | The levels observed in this study. |
| 3 | Average across modeled participant and stimulus differences. | The modeled participant and stimulus populations. |

We chose option 3 because our research question concerns average performance across
participant and stimulus populations, not only average-baseline or observed levels
([Hu et al., 1998](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9554609/);
[Hedeker et al., 2018](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5650580/)).

**Estimand sensitivity check.** Across visualization types, the largest difference
between the selected population-average probability and the zero-random-effect
probability was `r task1_conditional_gap_label`; the largest difference from the
fitted participant-and-stimulus average was `r task1_sample_gap_label`. The reporting
choice therefore does not materially change the pattern of results.

This does not make the sample representative of all EEG researchers.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Why participant-specific random slopes were not retained

We tested whether the effect of trial position differed between participants by adding
a participant-specific position slope: `(1 + position_c | ID)`, while retaining the ERP
pattern and stimulus terms. The model
`r if (task1_position_slope_singular) "produced a singular fit and could not" else "did not produce a singular fit, but could only"`
estimate this additional variation:

- The estimated variance of the position slopes was
  `r sprintf("%.5f", task1_position_slope_variance)`.

- The estimated correlation between the baseline accuracy and position slopes was
  `r sprintf("%.2f", task1_position_slope_correlation)`.

`r if (task1_position_slope_singular) "Together, these boundary estimates indicate that the data did not contain enough information to estimate participant baseline differences and participant-specific position effects separately." else "Although the fit was not singular, the estimated slope variation was very small and did not justify the additional model complexity."`

We also considered participant-specific effects for visualization type. However, each
participant provided only three responses for each visualization. Modeling the
seven-level visualization factor would require six additional slopes and their
covariances, which the available responses could not support reliably.

We therefore retained the simpler random-intercept model. This does not show that the
position and visualization effects are identical for every participant. It means only
that these data cannot reliably estimate how those effects differ between participants.
:::

```{r}
accuracy_estimates |>
  mutate(
    vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
    across(
      c(accuracy, lower_ci, upper_ci),
      \(x) scales::percent(x, accuracy = 0.1)
    )
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    col.names = c(
      "Visualization type",
      "Estimated accuracy",
      "Lower 95% CI",
      "Upper 95% CI"
    ),
    caption = "Population-average comparison-task accuracy",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Model:</strong> Binomial mixed-effects model with a logit link: ",
    "<code>correct ~ vistype + pattern + position_c + (1 | ID) + ",
    "(1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image)</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Reference visualization:</strong> Basic topoplot.</li>",
    "<li><strong>ERP pattern:</strong> Predictions were averaged equally across MMN, ",
    "N170, and P3.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Trial position:</strong> Predicted accuracy was calculated at the ",
    "average presentation position.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Random effects:</strong> Predictions were averaged across the modeled ",
    "distributions of participant baseline accuracy and target- and distractor-stimulus ",
    "difficulty.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Confidence intervals:</strong> A separate 95% confidence interval ",
    "was calculated for each visualization type from 10,000 simulated sets of ",
    "fixed-effect estimates generated with <code>MASS::mvrnorm()</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Limitation:</strong> The estimated participant and stimulus ",
    "random-intercept variances were treated as fixed when calculating these ",
    "intervals.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Model details"
)
```

```{r}
  scale_y_discrete(
    expand = expansion(add = 0.5),

      publication_labels <- c(
        basic = "Basic topoplot",

        bivariate_corner = "Bivariate corners",

        triple_CI = "Confidence intervals",
        uncert_markers = "Uncertainty markers",
        animation = "Animation"
      )
      unname(publication_labels[x])
    }
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(`FALSE` = "#222222", `TRUE` = "#377EB8"),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
    limits = comparison_accuracy_limits,
    breaks = scales::breaks_width(0.05),
    expand = expansion(mult = 0)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Comparison task accuracy",
    subtitle = "Population-average accuracy with 95% confidence intervals",
    x = "Model-estimated comparison-task accuracy",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_family = "Lato", base_size = 20) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
```

### Accuracy differences relative to Basic topoplot

- These comparisons estimate the population-average accuracy difference between each
  visualization and the basic topoplot. Confidence intervals crossing zero indicate
  that the corresponding visualization is not clearly different from Basic at the 95%
  confidence level.

```{r task1-basic-contrast-figure}
task1_basic_reference <- which(task1_vistype_levels == "basic")
task1_contrast_draws <- sweep(
  task1_population_draws,
  1,
  task1_population_draws[, task1_basic_reference],
  FUN = "-"
)
task1_contrast_estimates <-
  task1_estimand_comparison$population_average -
  task1_estimand_comparison$population_average[task1_basic_reference]
task1_contrast_intervals <- apply(
  task1_contrast_draws,
  2,
  quantile,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

task1_basic_contrasts <- tibble::tibble(
  vistype = factor(task1_vistype_levels, levels = task1_vistype_levels),
  difference = task1_contrast_estimates,
  lower_ci = task1_contrast_intervals[1, ],
  upper_ci = task1_contrast_intervals[2, ]
) |>
  filter(vistype != "basic") |>
  mutate(
    vistype = factor(vistype, levels = levels(accuracy_estimates$vistype))
  )

task1_contrast_limits <- c(
  max(-1, min(task1_basic_contrasts$lower_ci, na.rm = TRUE) - 0.03),
  min(1, max(task1_basic_contrasts$upper_ci, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.03)
)

task1_contrast_labels <- c(
  adjacent = "Adjacent plots",
  bivariate_corner = "Bivariate corners",

  uncert_markers = "Uncertainty markers",

)

) +
  geom_vline(

  ) +
```

### Model coefficients

- The coefficient table reports each visualization relative to the basic topoplot and
  reports the ERP-pattern and linear presentation-position effects. Coefficients are
  expressed as log odds.

```{r}
model_order <- glmmTMB(
  correct ~ vistype + pattern + position_c +
    (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image),
  family = binomial,
  data = task1_model
)

summary(model_order)$coefficients$cond |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("term") |>
  transmute(
    term = dplyr::recode(
      term,
      `(Intercept)` = "Basic topoplot (intercept)",
      vistypeadjacent = "Adjacent plots vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypeanimation = "Animation vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypebivariate_corner = "Bivariate corner vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypebivariate_range = "Bivariate range vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypetriple_CI = "Confidence intervals vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypeuncert_markers = "Uncertainty markers vs Basic topoplot",
      patternN170 = "N170 vs MMN pattern",
      patternP3 = "P3 vs MMN pattern",
      position_c = "Presentation position (centered)",
      .default = term
    ),
    estimate = Estimate,
    standard_error = .data[["Std. Error"]],
    z_value = .data[["z value"]],
    p_value = format_pvalue_html(.data[["Pr(>|z|)"]])
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
      "Term",
      "Estimate (log odds)",
      "Standard error",
      "z value",
      "p value"
    ),
    caption = paste(
      "Fixed effects for the comparison-task accuracy model.",
      "Values with p < .05 are shown in dark red."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Model:</strong> Binomial mixed-effects model with a logit link: ",
    "<code>correct ~ vistype + pattern + position_c + (1 | ID) + ",
    "(1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image)</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Reference visualization:</strong> Basic topoplot.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Reference ERP pattern:</strong> MMN.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Trial position:</strong> <code>position_c = 0</code> represents the ",
    "average presentation position.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Coefficient scale:</strong> Coefficients are reported as log odds, ",
    "not probabilities.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Model details"
)
```

### Overall test of visualization type

- A likelihood-ratio test compares the model containing visualization type with a reduced
  model that retains ERP pattern, presentation position, and the same random effects. It
  evaluates whether visualization type improves the model overall after these adjustments.

```{r}
model_no_vistype <- glmmTMB(
  correct ~ pattern + position_c +
    (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image),
  family = binomial,
  data = task1_model
)

model_vistype <- glmmTMB(
  correct ~ vistype + pattern + position_c +
    (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image),
  family = binomial,
  data = task1_model
)

anova_result <- anova(model_no_vistype, model_vistype) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("model") |>
  mutate(
    model = dplyr::recode(
      model,
      model_no_vistype = "Pattern and presentation position",
      model_vistype = "Pattern, position, and visualization type",
      .default = model
    )
  )

task1_vistype_lrt <- anova_result[2, ]

anova_result |>
  mutate(`Pr(>Chisq)` = format_pvalue_html(.data[["Pr(>Chisq)"]])) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
      "Model",
      "Parameters",
      "AIC",
      "BIC",
      "Log likelihood",
      "Deviance",
      "Likelihood-ratio chi-square",
      "df difference",
      "p value"
    ),
    caption = paste(
      "Likelihood-ratio test of visualization type for comparison-task accuracy.",
      "Values with p < .05 are shown in dark red."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Model family:</strong> Binomial mixed-effects models with a ",
    "logit link.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Full model:</strong> ",
    "<code>correct ~ vistype + pattern + position_c + (1 | ID) + ",
    "(1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image)</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Reduced model:</strong> ",
    "<code>correct ~ pattern + position_c + (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + ",
    "(1 | wrong_image)</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Comparison:</strong> The likelihood-ratio test evaluates whether ",
    "adding visualization type improves model fit.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Model comparison"
)
```

#### Model-comparison summary

Adding visualization type `r if (task1_vistype_lrt[["Pr(>Chisq)"]] < 0.05) "improved" else "did not clearly improve"`
the adjusted model, $\chi^2(`r task1_vistype_lrt[["Chi Df"]]`) =
`r sprintf("%.2f", task1_vistype_lrt[["Chisq"]])`$,
*p* = `r format.pval(task1_vistype_lrt[["Pr(>Chisq)"]], digits = 3, eps = 0.001)`.
The reduced and full models had AIC values of
`r sprintf("%.2f", anova_result$AIC[1])` and
`r sprintf("%.2f", anova_result$AIC[2])`, respectively. Thus, after accounting for ERP
pattern, presentation position, participant baseline accuracy, and target- and
distractor-stimulus difficulty, the analysis
`r if (task1_vistype_lrt[["Pr(>Chisq)"]] < 0.05) "provided evidence" else "did not provide clear evidence"`
that comparison-task accuracy differed overall among the seven visualization types.

### Model-estimated completion time

```{r task1-time-model}
task1_time_model <- task1_time %>%
  transmute(
    ID = factor(ID),
    vistype = relevel(factor(vistype), ref = "basic"),
    position = as.integer(position),
    time_sec = as.numeric(time_sec)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(ID),
    !is.na(vistype),
    !is.na(position),
    !is.na(time_sec),
    time_sec > 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(position_c = position - mean(position))

task1_time_fit <- lmer(
  log(time_sec) ~ vistype + position_c + (1 | ID),
  data = task1_time_model
)

time_estimates <- emmeans(
  task1_time_fit,
  ~ vistype,
  type = "response"
) %>%
  confint() %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  transmute(
    vistype,
    estimated_time = response,
    lower_ci = lower.CL,
    upper_ci = upper.CL
  ) %>%
  arrange(estimated_time) %>%
  mutate(vistype = factor(vistype, levels = vistype))

time_estimates |>
  mutate(
    vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
    across(
      c(estimated_time, lower_ci, upper_ci),
      \(x) round(x, 1)
    )
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    col.names = c(
      "Visualization type",
      "Estimated time (seconds)",
      "Lower 95% CI",
      "Upper 95% CI"
    ),
    caption = "Model-estimated comparison-task completion time",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Model:</strong> Gaussian linear mixed model for log completion ",
    "time: <code>log(time_sec) ~ vistype + position_c + (1 | ID)</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Reference visualization:</strong> Basic topoplot.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Trial position:</strong> Estimates were calculated at the average ",
    "presentation position.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Output scale:</strong> Estimates and 95% confidence intervals were ",
    "back-transformed from log time to seconds.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Model details"
)
```

### Association between completion time and accuracy

The following analyses ask whether longer completion times were associated with greater
accuracy. They describe associations and do not establish that spending more time caused
participants to answer correctly.

```{r task1-time-accuracy-association}
task1_time_accuracy <- task1_time_model %>%
  select(ID, vistype, position, position_c, time_sec) %>%
  left_join(
    task1_model %>%
      select(ID, position, correct, pattern, stimulus, wrong_image),
    by = c("ID", "position")
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(task1_time_accuracy) == nrow(task1_time_model),
  !anyNA(task1_time_accuracy$correct)
)

task1_time_accuracy_counts <- task1_time_accuracy %>%
  count(ID, name = "trials")

stopifnot(
  nrow(task1_time_accuracy_counts) == 114,
  all(task1_time_accuracy_counts$trials == 21)
)

task1_time_accuracy <- task1_time_accuracy %>%
  mutate(log_time = log(time_sec)) %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  mutate(
    participant_mean_log_time = mean(log_time),
    log_time_within = log_time - participant_mean_log_time
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    log_time_between_c = participant_mean_log_time -
      mean(participant_mean_log_time)
  )

task1_participant_time_accuracy <- task1_time_accuracy %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  summarise(
    accuracy = mean(correct),
    typical_time_sec = exp(mean(log_time)),
    mean_log_time = mean(log_time),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

task1_time_accuracy_correlation <- cor.test(
  task1_participant_time_accuracy$mean_log_time,
  task1_participant_time_accuracy$accuracy,
  method = "pearson"
)

task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table <- tibble::tibble(
  participants = nrow(task1_participant_time_accuracy),
  correlation = unname(task1_time_accuracy_correlation$estimate),
  lower_ci = task1_time_accuracy_correlation$conf.int[1],
  upper_ci = task1_time_accuracy_correlation$conf.int[2],
  p_value = task1_time_accuracy_correlation$p.value
)

task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table %>%
  transmute(
    Participants = participants,
    `Pearson r` = sprintf("%.3f", correlation),
    `Lower 95% CI` = sprintf("%.3f", lower_ci),
    `Upper 95% CI` = sprintf("%.3f", upper_ci),
    `p value` = format_pvalue_html(p_value)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    caption = paste(
      "Participant-level correlation between accuracy and typical",
      "completion time"
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Unit:</strong> One record per participant (N = 114).</li>",
    "<li><strong>Accuracy:</strong> Proportion correct across 21 trials.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Typical time:</strong> Mean log completion time, equivalent to the ",
    "log of the participant's geometric mean time.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Interpretation:</strong> The correlation asks whether participants ",
    "who were generally slower were also generally more accurate.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Correlation details"
)

task1_time_accuracy_fit <- glmer(
  correct ~ log_time_within + log_time_between_c + vistype + pattern +
    position_c + (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image),
  data = task1_time_accuracy,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)

task1_time_accuracy_coefficients <- summary(
  task1_time_accuracy_fit
)$coefficients

task1_time_accuracy_effects <- tibble::tibble(
  term = c("log_time_within", "log_time_between_c"),
  comparison = c(
    "Within participants: twice the usual trial time",
    "Between participants: twice the typical completion time"
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    estimate = task1_time_accuracy_coefficients[term, "Estimate"],
    standard_error = task1_time_accuracy_coefficients[term, "Std. Error"],
    odds_ratio = exp(estimate * log(2)),
    lower_ci = exp((estimate - 1.96 * standard_error) * log(2)),
    upper_ci = exp((estimate + 1.96 * standard_error) * log(2)),
    p_value = task1_time_accuracy_coefficients[term, "Pr(>|z|)"]
  )

task1_time_accuracy_effects %>%
  transmute(
    Association = comparison,
    `Odds ratio` = sprintf("%.3f", odds_ratio),
    `Lower 95% CI` = sprintf("%.3f", lower_ci),
    `Upper 95% CI` = sprintf("%.3f", upper_ci),
    `p value` = format_pvalue_html(p_value)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    caption = "Adjusted association between completion time and trial accuracy",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Model:</strong> Binomial mixed-effects model with a logit link: ",
    "<code>correct ~ log_time_within + log_time_between_c + vistype + ",
    "pattern + position_c + (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + ",
    "(1 | wrong_image)</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Within-participant effect:</strong> Compares a participant's ",
    "longer and shorter trials.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Between-participant effect:</strong> Compares participants with ",
    "different typical completion times.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Adjustment:</strong> Visualization type, ERP pattern, presentation ",
    "position, participant baseline accuracy, and target- and distractor-stimulus ",
    "difficulty.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Effect scale:</strong> Odds ratios compare a doubling of completion ",
    "time; values above 1 indicate greater odds of a correct response.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Model details"
)
```

At the participant level, accuracy and typical completion time had a Pearson correlation
of `r sprintf("%.3f", task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$correlation)`
(95% CI
`r sprintf("%.3f", task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$lower_ci)` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$upper_ci)`,
*p* = `r format_pvalue_html(task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$p_value)`). In the
adjusted mixed model, doubling the time spent on a trial was associated with an odds
ratio of
`r sprintf("%.3f", task1_time_accuracy_effects$odds_ratio[1])` for a correct response
(95% CI `r sprintf("%.3f", task1_time_accuracy_effects$lower_ci[1])` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", task1_time_accuracy_effects$upper_ci[1])`). The between-participant
odds ratio was `r sprintf("%.3f", task1_time_accuracy_effects$odds_ratio[2])`
(95% CI `r sprintf("%.3f", task1_time_accuracy_effects$lower_ci[2])` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", task1_time_accuracy_effects$upper_ci[2])`).

All three estimates were small, and their intervals included the corresponding null
value (zero for the correlation and one for the odds ratios). These data therefore
provide little evidence that longer completion time was meaningfully associated with
greater Task 1 accuracy.

```{r task1-time-accuracy-summary}
task1_time_accuracy_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  analysis = c(
    "Overall participant correlation",
    "Within participants",
    "Between participants (adjusted)"
  ),
  estimate = c(
    sprintf(
      "r = %.3f (95%% CI %.3f to %.3f)",
      task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$correlation,
      task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$lower_ci,
      task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$upper_ci
    ),
    sprintf(
      "OR = %.3f (95%% CI %.3f to %.3f)",
      task1_time_accuracy_effects$odds_ratio[1],
      task1_time_accuracy_effects$lower_ci[1],
      task1_time_accuracy_effects$upper_ci[1]
    ),
    sprintf(
      "OR = %.3f (95%% CI %.3f to %.3f)",
      task1_time_accuracy_effects$odds_ratio[2],
      task1_time_accuracy_effects$lower_ci[2],
      task1_time_accuracy_effects$upper_ci[2]
    )
  ),
  p_value = c(
    task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$p_value,
    task1_time_accuracy_effects$p_value
  ),
  summary = c(
    paste(
      "Slower participants were only slightly more accurate;",
      "the data also support no association."
    ),
    paste(
      "For the same participant, spending twice as long on a trial was not",
      "clearly associated with greater accuracy."
    ),
    paste(
      "Participants with twice the typical completion time were not clearly",
      "more accurate after adjustment."
    )
  )
)

task1_time_accuracy_summary %>%
  transmute(
    Analysis = analysis,
    `Estimate (95% CI)` = estimate,
    `p value` = format_pvalue_html(p_value),
    `Plain-language summary` = summary
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    caption = "Short summary of completion-time and accuracy results",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```
